evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.9. (M. Bialy) Assume that a plane billiard has a family of rotational invar iant circles with all the rotation numbers in the interval (0, 1/2). Then the billiard table is an ellipse. A variation on Innami's result is the following question, suggested by V. Kaloshin:

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a strictly convex planar domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and consider the associated Birkhoff billiard map $T$ defined on the phase cylinder of inward unit tangent vectors based on $\partial\Omega$, parametrized so that the canonical rotation number takes values in $[0,1/2]$ (rotation number $1/2$ corresponding to the boundary itself). A rotational invariant circle of $T$ is an essential (non-contractible) $T$-invariant closed curve in the phase cylinder; on such a curve the dynamics is conjugate to a rigid rotation with a well-defined rotation number.

Conjecture: Suppose that the billiard map associated with $\Omega$ admits a family of rotational invariant circles whose rotation numbers fill the entire open interval $(0, 1/2)$. Prove that $\partial\Omega$ must be an ellipse.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture remains open in general. Significant partial progress has been made: Bialy and Mironov established the Birkhoff–Poritsky conjecture for centrally symmetric C²-smooth convex planar billiards (Annals of Mathematics, 2022), and proved that if a neighborhood of the boundary admits a C¹-smooth foliation by convex caustics with rotation numbers in (0, 1/4], then the boundary is an ellipse. Kaloshin and collaborators have proved the Birkhoff conjecture for domains nearly centrally symmetric or close to an ellipse. The full conjecture as stated (requiring all rotation numbers in (0, 1/2)) has not been fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: The Birkhoff-Poritsky conjecture for centrally-symmetric billiard tables
status_evidence.snippet: Bialy and Mironov proved the Birkhoff-Poritsky conjecture for centrally-symmetric C²-smooth convex planar billiards, showing the boundary is an ellipse under foliation by caustics with rotation numbers in (0,1/4].
status_evidence.claim: The centrally-symmetric case has been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Integrable Billiards and Related Topics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey by Bialy and Mironov discussing the status of conjectures on integrable billiards and invariant curves.
status_evidence.claim: The general Birkhoff/Bialy conjecture remains a central open problem.

status_evidence.title: Birkhoff Conjecture for nearly centrally symmetric domains
status_evidence.snippet: Kaloshin et al. extend results to nearly centrally symmetric domains.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress under perturbative assumptions.
